roadmap.goal: Lighthouse decides for itself whether a settings edit changed what gets fetched. A hash over thirteen properties - what the query asks the tracker for UNION how the answer is read into the stored record - is written at the end of every cycle and compared at the start of the next one; a mismatch makes the next cycle `mode=full` and the summary line says `reason=configuration-changed`. Everything outside the set costs no remote call at all. The same thirteen properties also become the ONE list the save-time purge decision reads, and that purge narrows from five triggers to one: a connection change, the only edit `removed = stored - fetched` cannot reconcile. Ungated - with delta off the fingerprint is inert, not inactive.

phases.name: One list, one hash, one column
phases.description: The SSOT the rest of the slice points at, built bottom-up and landed before anything consumes it. `FetchFingerprint` ships from DISTILL as a real type with EMPTY registries and a throwing `For(...)` (DT5-5) - deliberately, because an empty registry is what makes guard G2 a genuine red rather than a table agreeing with itself. Fill the registries first (01-01), so every later step has one place to point at and one test that fails when the pointing goes stale; then the hash itself as a pure function with its own unit test (01-02); then persistence, so a cycle records what it asked for (01-03). Nothing in this phase changes what any cycle downloads: the three `fetchShapeChanged: false` literals are still hard-coded, so the column fills and behaviour is unchanged. That is on purpose - it means the hash can be got wrong and corrected without a single scenario's mode assertion moving.

steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.1 (widened) / ADR-140's Decision section, contract shape `pure-function`. THE ONE DESIGN QUESTION DISTILL'S SCAFFOLD DOES NOT ANSWER, and it will bite at 04-01 if it is ducked here: the scaffolded signature is `For(IWorkItemQueryOwner queryOwner)`, and that interface reaches only TWELVE of the thirteen groups. `Models/IWorkItemQueryOwner.cs` exposes DataRetrievalValue, WorkItemTypes, ToDoStates, DoingStates, DoneStates, StateMappings, DoneItemsCutoffDays and ParentOverrideAdditionalFieldDefinitionId, and it inherits WorkTrackingSystemConnectionId + WorkTrackingSystemConnection from `IWorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner` (which is where the connection's AdditionalFieldDefinitions and WorkTrackingSystem are reachable). `FeatureOwnerAdditionalFieldDefinitionId` and `SizeEstimateAdditionalFieldDefinitionId` are declared on `Portfolio` (`Models/Portfolio.cs:19,21`) and on NOTHING the interface can see. Resolve it with a pattern match inside `For` (`if (queryOwner is Portfolio portfolio) { ... }`) - one entry point, one registry, and G2 keeps pinning it. Do NOT widen `IWorkItemQueryOwner` with portfolio-only members (Team implements it too, and the members would be dead surface on the team half) and do NOT add a `For(Portfolio)` overload: two entry points make G2's single registry stop meaning one function, and S4136 is error-severity in this repo. If you skip this, scenario 4's `which field names the owning team` and `which field carries the size estimate` cases are the two that go red at 04-01, and they will read as a portfolio-wiring bug rather than a reach bug. Hashing: collections hash ORDER-INSENSITIVELY (ADR-140), which for `StateMappings` means order-insensitive over the mappings AND over each mapping's `States` - scenario 8 reverses WorkItemTypes and all three state columns, and `TeamExtensions.StateMappingsChanged` is index-wise today, so do not copy that comparison's shape. `AdditionalFieldDefinitions` is a `List<AdditionalFieldDefinition>`, so project it to a stable, order-insensitive rendering of the fields that decide what is requested and stored, not to object identity or EF ids alone. Verified so you do not have to: BOTH `TeamRepository.GetAll` (`:21-26`) and `PortfolioRepository.GetAllProjectsWithIncludes` (`:63-65`) eagerly `Include` the connection with its `AdditionalFieldDefinitions`, so the sync scope really can see them - scenario 7 is not going to fail on a missing EF include. The hash must be STABLE across processes and releases: no `GetHashCode()` on strings or collections (randomised per process in .NET, so the stored fingerprint would mismatch after every restart and every cycle would be full forever) and no `Guid`/timestamp in the input. A rendered, sorted, delimited string run through a deterministic digest is the shape. Watch the column: `FetchFingerprint` is `string?` on `WorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner` with no length constraint declared, so keep the output short and fixed-width rather than storing the rendered input. Tests are NUnit, example-based, `[TestCaseSource]` for the thirteen `changes the hash` cases; Moq is not needed here - the function takes entities, not ports. New test file, so the analyzer filter MUST union `git status --porcelain` (ci-learnings recurrence 3: seven new violations in one brand-new test file went unread because `git diff` cannot see it). Preflight and gates exactly as in 01-01; expect skipped to stay at 48 and passed to rise.

The value written is the one computed for THIS cycle's configuration - computed once per cycle, not once per phase
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.1 (the storage half) / ADR-140, contract shape `bounded-change` (declared mutation: one nullable column per entity per cycle). DISTILL's recorded red for scenario 8 is the POSITIVE CONTROL, not the mode: `Assert.That(before, Is.Not.Null.And.Not.Empty)` inside `ThenTheTeamsFingerprintIsUnchangedBy` - with nothing stored, `the fingerprint did not change` compared null to null and passed, which is the vacuous assertion the gate caught and fixed. So this step is red on `nothing was ever recorded`, and the order-insensitivity claim only becomes real once it is green. THE ASYMMETRY THAT WILL COST YOU AN HOUR IF YOU ASSUME SYMMETRY: the portfolio's sync-owned write is `portfolio.RefreshUpdateTime()` at `WorkItemService.cs:44`, inside `UpdateFeaturesForPortfolio` - the fingerprint write belongs right beside it, and ADR-140's whole argument is that `UpdateTime` already proves a sync write to a concurrency-tokened config aggregate is safe here (`RegenerateConcurrencyTokens` rotates only for `EntityState.Added`, `LighthouseAppContext.cs:572-579`). The TEAM has no such line in `WorkItemService`: `team.RefreshUpdateTime()` lives in `TeamMetricsService.cs:785`, which runs AFTER `UpdateWorkItemsForTeam` inside `TeamDataService.UpdateTeamData`. Do not move it and do not put the fingerprint there - metrics is the wrong home for a fetch decision. `WorkItemService` already injects `IRepository<Team> teamRepository` (constructor arg 6), so the team write needs no new dependency; make sure it is actually SAVED - the harness reads the column back through `IRepository<Team>.GetById` in a FRESH scope (`FasterUpdatesAcceptanceTest.cs:972-982`), so an in-memory assignment that never reaches the database will fail the assertion while looking correct in the debugger. Compute the fingerprint ONCE per cycle and use the same value for the comparison (02-01) and the write: recomputing between them is harmless today but makes a later reader believe the two can differ. Do NOT write the fingerprint from the parent-Feature path (`ResolveRemoteParentFeatureFetch`, `:1008`) - parents share the portfolio's fingerprint and a second write there would be the same value twice, or worse, a different one. Do NOT touch the three `fetchShapeChanged: false` literals in this step: this commit must leave every mode assertion in the whole suite exactly where it was, which is what makes it safe to correct the hash afterwards. No model change here, therefore no migration - the column landed with the precursor (31b94e13a). Preflight and gates as in 01-01; skipped goes 48 -> 47.

steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.5 / D8, contract shape `bounded-change`. This step may need NO production change beyond 02-01 - a null stored fingerprint is a mismatch, and a mismatch is Full. Un-ignore it and RUN it; if green, record the run in the commit message rather than inventing work. What it is actually guarding is the tempting shape `if (stored is null) return false; // nothing to compare` - which is safe-looking and is exactly the bug D8 exists to forbid: an upgraded instance would run delta against nothing and serve whatever the previous release stored, forever. DT5-10 explains why this scenario can fail for the right reason at all: `GivenTheTeamsWorkWasStoredByAReleaseThatKnewNothingOfFingerprints` seeds work that ALREADY CARRIES remote change stamps, so slice 02's `any stored record without a stamp resolves to Full` branch cannot be what makes the cycle full - the only thing missing is the fingerprint. Do not `simplify` the seeding. The third criterion is currently vacuous and becomes real in 02-03: `ThenTheOperatorIsNotToldConfigurationIsWhy` asserts `Does.Not.Contain("configuration-changed")`, and nothing prints that token yet. RE-RUN THIS SCENARIO AT 02-03 - it is the assertion that stops the reason from being printed unconditionally whenever the mode is Full, and it is the reason 02-03 has to distinguish `never recorded` from `changed`. DISTILL already ran an absence-assertion audit over this fixture and fixed scenario 11 by adding `ThenTheOperatorSeesAFullUpdate(3, 3)` before the absence claim, so the line it reads is already proven to carry mode, scanned and fetched (DT5-16). steps.name: The operator is told that configuration is why
criteria: A cycle that ran Full because the fingerprint changed prints the token `reason=configuration-changed` on its one summary line

The token rides on the same summary line as mode, scanned, fetched, duration and success, and the other five tokens are unchanged
The persisted refresh log row gains no new field
The reason travels from where the mode is decided to where the line is written, without a second decision being made at the log site
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.2 / DT5-8 / the amended Summary-Line Contract. THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT, and the one a fast implementation gets wrong: `reason=configuration-changed` must be printed when the fingerprint CHANGED and must NOT be printed when there was never one. Both are `stored != computed` if you write the comparison naively, and scenario 11's `ThenTheOperatorIsNotToldConfigurationIsWhy` (`Does.Not.Contain("configuration-changed")`) is what fails. So the mode input stays one boolean (`fetchShapeChanged`, true in both cases - D8's expensive answer) while the reason distinguishes them: `null stored` is `no reason`, `stored and different` is the configuration reason. Un-ignore scenario 2 AND re-run scenario 11 in this same commit; if 11 goes red here the reason is being derived from the mode rather than from the cause. Where the token rides: `Models/SyncOutcome.cs` is `public sealed record SyncOutcome(SyncMode Mode, int RecordsScanned, int RecordsFetched)`, constructed POSITIONALLY in several places and returned all the way from `WorkItemService` through `ITeamDataService`/`IWorkItemService` to both updaters. It is a shared contract, so extend it the way CLAUDE.md asks: add an optional `init` member with a default rather than a fourth positional parameter, so every existing construction site - including `SyncOutcome.None` - keeps compiling untouched and the blast radius stays at the two updaters plus `LogUpdateSummary`. Grep for `SyncOutcome` before you edit it. `UpdateServiceBase.LogUpdateSummary` (`:59-64`) is the ONE place the line is written, for both entities - do not add a second log call in either updater. Field ORDER is not asserted: the specifications use `Does.Contain` per token (`ModeField`, `ScannedField`, `FetchedField`, `ReasonField` are separate constants), so put `reason=` wherever it reads best; do NOT print an empty `reason=` when there is no reason, because `ThenTheOperatorIsNotToldConfigurationIsWhy` only forbids the VALUE but a bare `reason=` is noise on every line the epic just cleaned up. `RefreshLog` gains NO `Reason` column (DT5-8) - `ThenTheRefreshReported` asserts Mode, RecordsScanned, RecordsFetched and Success and nothing else, and a second migration to persist a token nothing queries is schema for its own sake; both updaters build their `RefreshLog` in a `finally` and those blocks stay as they are. `configuration-changed` is the ONLY reason value this slice needs. Stryker: the summary-line template already carries `Stryker disable once all` comments on its neighbouring Debug traces because slice 01 pinned the wording here - do not add the token to a trace line, add it to the pinned summary. Preflight and gates as in 01-01; skipped goes 45 -> 44.

phases.name: A save stops throwing away history - and only then can the widened set be measured
phases.description: The phase that diverges from the DISTILL Handoff's suggested order, deliberately. The Handoff puts the widened set (scenarios 3, 5, 6, 7) before the purge narrowing; that order cannot work. Scenarios 5 and 6 assert `the team kept the history it recorded` BEFORE the refresh, and today a state or state-mapping edit trips `TeamExtensions.WorkItemRelatedSettingsChanged`, so `TeamController.UpdateTeam:178` deletes every stored work item for the team and the cascade on `WorkItemStateTransition.WorkItemId` takes the history with it. Worse, six of scenario 3's eight cases download the whole query TODAY for exactly that reason - the team has nothing stored, so the resolver answers Full without the fingerprint being consulted at all. Taking the widened set first therefore means writing the fingerprint against six tests that go green either way: the same wrong-reason-green the DISTILL gate caught twice in this fixture. So the purge narrows first (03-01, 03-02), and the widened set is measured against a save that no longer answers the question by deleting the evidence (03-03, 03-04). Within the narrowing, the Handoff's own ordering is load-bearing and preserved: the DON'T-purge half (15, 17) before the DO-purge half (14, 16), because 14 passes today and taking it first would mean writing the narrowing against a test that cannot see it.

steps.name: A query edit keeps the history and the Features already stored
criteria: Changing a team's query no longer deletes that team's stored work items or their recorded state transitions - the rendered history is byte-identical across the save
The next cycle after that edit still downloads the whole query and reports Full with 3 scanned / 3 fetched, so the widened query really does take effect
Changing a portfolio's query leaves the portfolio holding the same three Features it held before, and that cycle records the portfolio's new fingerprint
The save-time purge decision reads the one registered set, not a second list of its own
A connection change still purges on the team side - the existing behaviour is narrowed, not removed
steps.implementation_notes: A2 / DT5-2, contract shape `unbounded-preservation` on both - their defining claim is an ABSENCE (nothing stored was thrown away), which is why DISTILL gave each a positive control. THIS IS THE USER-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THE SLICE SHIPS, and nobody wrote the current behaviour down, so nobody will notice it changed: today `TeamController.UpdateTeam:178` calls `team.WorkItemRelatedSettingsChanged(teamSetting)` and on true runs `workItemRepository.RemoveWorkItemsForTeam(team.Id)`, deleting the team's stored work items AND their transition history. After this step only a connection change does. What replaces it is `removed = stored - fetched` on the next full cycle, which is how the portfolio side has always reconciled the same edit without a purge. A release-note line is OWED at slice close (slice brief, `Behaviour change this slice ships`). WHAT `WorkItemRelatedSettingsChanged` LOOKS LIKE TODAY (`API/Helpers/TeamExtensions.cs:65-79`): it ORs five comparisons - queryChanged, connectionChanged, workItemTypesChanged, statesChanged, stateMappingsChanged. Four of the five go; only `connectionChanged` earns the purge. `FetchFingerprint.PropertiesThatAlsoCostAFreshStart` is the SSOT for which ones those are, and G2 is what keeps the two in step - so read the registry rather than deleting four lines and leaving a hard-coded comparison behind. Name the narrowed method for what it now decides; the old name describes the old, wider question. THE ASYMMETRY THAT IS NOT A BUG (DISTILL upstream issue 2, ADR-140 Consequences): the save-time consumer compares an entity against an incoming settings DTO, which carries no connection field definitions and no work tracking system, so three of the thirteen rows are permanently invisible to it. G2 asserts the SET, not that both consumers can reach every member. Do not try to make the controller see them. Scenario 15's red is the history (`TheHistoryOf(history.WorkItemId)` returns `<string.Empty>` today because the purge already ran); scenario 17's red is the portfolio fingerprint being null - which 01-03 and 02-01 should already have fixed, so 17 may well be GREEN on arrival. That is expected and is the point of doing both entities' wiring in phase 01/02: un-ignore it, RUN it, and record the run in the commit message rather than inventing work. Do NOT touch `PortfolioController` in this step - the portfolio's purge is 03-02's, and adding it here would make scenario 17's `the portfolio still has all three Features` pass for the trivial reason that nothing purges the portfolio yet. Regression watch: `TeamsControllerTest` / the team settings tests almost certainly pin the current purge behaviour on a query or state edit. If one goes red, it is asserting the behaviour this step deliberately changes - update it and say so in the commit body, do not weaken the new behaviour to keep it green. Preflight and gates as in 01-01; skipped goes 44 -> 42.

steps.name: A connection change starts from nothing, on both entities
criteria: Moving a team to a different connection leaves that team with no stored work items and no stored transitions for them, and the next cycle reports Full with 3 scanned / 3 fetched
Moving a portfolio to a different connection leaves the portfolio claiming no Features, and the next cycle reports Full with 3 scanned / 3 fetched
A Feature another portfolio still claims survives the move - the moving portfolio drops its claim, it does not delete somebody else's row
Scenarios 15 and 17 are re-run in this commit and stay green: the narrowing did not narrow too far
Both entities answer the one question the same way
steps.implementation_notes: A2 / DT5-2, contract shape `bounded-change` on both. WHY THIS EDIT AND ONLY THIS EDIT EARNS A PURGE: the same reference id on a different tracker is a DIFFERENT item, and `SyncWorkItem` updates the stored copy IN PLACE - so without a purge the old system's transition history silently becomes the new system's. That is the one case `removed = stored - fetched` cannot reconcile, because the ids match. Scenario 14 is GREEN OFF SHIPPED CODE and DISTILL declared it as such rather than manufacturing a red: `TeamController.UpdateTeam:178` already purges on a connection change and the cascade on `WorkItemStateTransition.WorkItemId` already takes the history. It ships as the regression guard on the one behaviour 03-01 keeps - the risk in this slice is narrowing too far - and its positive control is scenario 15, which was red. Un-ignore it, RUN it, record the run. THE PORTFOLIO HALF IS THE REAL WORK, and `PortfolioController.UpdatePortfolio` (`:96`, the body at `:134-150`) has no change detection at all today: it syncs and saves. Give it the equivalent, reading the same `FetchFingerprint.PropertiesThatAlsoCostAFreshStart` the team half reads - one question, two entities, one answer. WHAT `starting from nothing` MEANS FOR A PORTFOLIO, and getting this wrong deletes other people's data: the assertion is `TheFeaturesInThePortfolio(portfolioId)`, which reads `portfolio.Features` through `IRepository<Portfolio>` (`FasterUpdatesAcceptanceTest.cs:823-829`). So DROP THE PORTFOLIO'S CLAIMS - do not hard-delete Feature rows. A Feature can be claimed by more than one portfolio (slice 03 phase 05 added the two boundary scenarios for exactly this), and the existing `IOrphanedFeatureCleanupService.CleanupAsync`, which `PortfolioUpdater` runs in its own `finally` (`:121-125`), already hard-deletes `!IsParentFeature && !Portfolios.Any()` with `SweepDepartedFeatureSpells` closing the open blocked spells on the way. Dropping the claim is therefore both sufficient for the assertion and correct for the shared case; deleting rows directly would take a Feature another portfolio still holds. Note the assertion runs BEFORE the refresh, so the claim must be dropped at SAVE time, not deferred to the next cycle. Do not reach for `PortfolioRepository.Remove` - that is the delete-the-portfolio path and it removes orphaned Features as a side effect. Re-run scenarios 15 and 17 in this commit; if 15 reds here, the narrowing has been widened back by whatever shape the portfolio half borrowed. Preflight and gates as in 01-01; skipped goes 42 -> 40.

steps.name: Every fetch-shaping team setting, as one table
criteria: All eight cases pass: the query text, the work item types, each of the three state columns, the finished-work cutoff, the parent-naming field and a state mapping
Each case downloads the whole query exactly once, issues no by-reference-id fetches, and reports Full with 3 scanned / 3 fetched
Each case prints `reason=configuration-changed`
Each case is now full because the fingerprint changed, not because a purge emptied storage - none of the eight trips a purge after 03-01
The cutoff case and the parent-field case in particular go from downloading nothing to downloading everything
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.1 / AC-5.2, contract shape `bounded-change`, eight cases via `[TestCaseSource(nameof(EveryTeamSettingThatChangesWhatIsFetched))]`. WHY THIS STEP IS HERE AND NOT AT THE HANDOFF'S POSITION 5: DISTILL's RED run recorded `6 of 8 on Does.Contain("reason=configuration-changed"); the cutoff and parent-field cases on FullDownloadsIssued -> Expected: 1 But was: 0`. Read that carefully - six of the eight cases ALREADY download the whole query today, and not because of any fingerprint: the query, types, state-column and state-mapping edits all trip `WorkItemRelatedSettingsChanged`, storage is emptied, and `SyncModeResolver` answers Full on its `nothing stored` branch. Run before 03-01 and 03-02, this step would go green on six cases with a fingerprint that does nothing. After the narrowing it discriminates, which is the whole point. The two cases that were genuinely red from the start - `how far back finished work still counts` (`DoneItemsCutoffDays`) and `which field names the parent` (`ParentOverrideAdditionalFieldDefinitionId`) - are the live gap A2 named: both demonstrably shape the remote query and neither triggers anything today. `WorkTrackingSystemConnectionId` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from this table (DT5-9): it also purges, so `nothing is stored` would be a second, independent reason for the next cycle to be full and the row would stop discriminating. It has scenario 14 instead. Do not add it. Expect little or no production change here if 01-02 read all thirteen registered properties - `FetchFingerprint.cs` is listed as where a fix would land, not as a promise of an edit. If a case is red, the fix belongs in `For(...)`, never in the scenario and never by adding a special case to the resolver. If you find yourself editing `Slice05FetchFingerprintSpecifications.cs`, stop: DISTILL owns the specifications (ADR-025) and the table is the acceptance criterion, not a fixture detail. Preflight and gates as in 01-01. Skip arithmetic: the 49 baseline counts CASES, not methods, so lifting this one `[Ignore]` drops eight at once - skipped goes 40 -> 32.

steps.name: The three edits that leave the request byte-identical
criteria: Re-assigning the same raw states across different mappings leaves what the tracker is asked for identical and still makes the next cycle download the whole query
Moving a state from one column to another leaves what the tracker is asked for identical and still makes the next cycle download the whole query
Adding a field definition to the CONNECTION - changing no property of the team at all - still makes the next cycle download the whole query for a team on that connection
In all three the request-unchanged control is asserted first and holds: these are not query changes wearing a disguise
The first two keep the team's recorded history across the save - they are state edits, and state edits no longer purge
All three report Full with 3 scanned / 3 fetched
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.1 (widened) / DT5-1 - these three ARE the wave's substantive finding, and a fingerprint built from what `PrepareQuery` is handed passes scenarios 1-4 and fails all three. Batched into one step on purpose: three separate steps would carry an identical AC structure (edit X, request unchanged, whole query downloaded), which the decomposition rule forbids at 3+, and they share one production concern - whether `For(...)` reaches past the request into how the answer is READ. Three mechanisms, all verified in code, none to re-derive. (1) SCENARIO 5, state-mapping RE-ASSIGNMENT: `JiraWorkTrackingConnector.CreateWorkItemFromJiraIssue:1313,1316` stores `MapRawStateToMappedName(issue.State)` and `MapStateToStateCategory(issue.State)`, both of which walk `GetRawStatesForCategory`. The edit redistributes the SAME raw states across different mappings - `WhenTheOperatorReadsOneRawStateAsADifferentState` moves `Test` from the `In Progress` mapping to the `Done` mapping - so the raw state set, and therefore `AllStates` and the query, do not move while the stored State and StateCategory of every record in it do. Note the correction DISTILL made to the maintainer's stated mechanism: a mapping RENAME is visible (`GetRawStatesForCategory` resolves a mapping by NAME from the category list, so an un-renamed category entry falls through to the literal and `AllStates` does change). Re-assignment is the invisible one. (2) SCENARIO 6, a state moving between columns: `WorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner.AllStates` is a `Union` of the three columns, so `DoingStates = [In Progress]` + `DoneStates = [Done, In Review]` yields the same union as before and re-categorises every stored record in `In Review`. This is the scenario that fails if the three columns were collapsed to `AllStates` at 01-01 - AC-5.1 as briefed names `AllStates`, and that is the bug. (3) SCENARIO 7, a CONNECTION field definition: `JiraWorkTrackingConnector:1300,1320,1361` and `AzureDevOpsWorkTrackingConnector:577,609` - adding a definition changes what is requested AND what is stored in `AdditionalFieldValues` for every entity on the connection, while `WorkTrackingSystemConnectionId` never moves. This is the one no save-time comparison can EVER catch, so its only detector is the sync-time fingerprint; `WhenTheOperatorAddsAFieldToTheConnection` seeds the definition directly on the connection rather than through the settings PUT, precisely because a settings DTO cannot carry it. Both repositories already eagerly include the connection's `AdditionalFieldDefinitions` (`TeamRepository.cs:21-26`, `PortfolioRepository.cs:63-65`), so a red here is a hashing-reach problem, not an EF include problem. Scenarios 5 and 6 also assert `ThenTheTeamKeptTheHistoryItRecorded` BEFORE the refresh - that is 03-01's narrowing, and if it reds here the narrowing regressed. Fixes belong in `For(...)`; do not touch the scenarios or the specifications. Preflight and gates as in 01-01; three `[Ignore]`s, one case each, so skipped goes 32 -> 29.

phases.name: The portfolio half, the free list, and the guard that closes the surface
phases.description: What is left once the team half is proven: the portfolio's own three fetch-shaping settings, the two independence guards that only guard once both halves exist, AC-5.3's free list - which is the half of the epic that is easiest to lose and is deliberately last, because it is vacuous until a fingerprint exists that could have invalidated - and finally G1, in a commit of its own. The ordering inside this phase is the Handoff's, unchanged: scenario 4, then 12 and 13, then 9 and 10, then G1.

steps.name: Every fetch-shaping portfolio setting, including the two only a portfolio has
criteria: All ten cases pass, including the two the team half does not have: the field that names the owning team and the field that carries the size estimate
Each case downloads the whole Feature query exactly once, issues no by-reference-id Feature fetches, and reports Full with 3 scanned / 3 fetched
Each case prints `reason=configuration-changed`
The portfolio's fingerprint is computed from the portfolio's own configuration, including the two portfolio-only field references
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.1 / AC-5.2 / AC-5.6, contract shape `bounded-change`, ten cases via `[TestCaseSource(nameof(EveryPortfolioSettingThatChangesWhatIsFetched))]`. DISTILL's RED run: all 10 failed on `FullFeatureDownloadsIssued -> Expected: 1 But was: 0`, i.e. purely the wiring - which 02-01 filled at `WorkItemService.cs:799`. So expect this to be LARGELY A VERIFICATION STEP, and if it is, record the run in the commit message rather than inventing work. THE TWO CASES THAT CAN STILL FAIL, and they are the payoff of 01-02's interface note: `which field names the owning team` (`FeatureOwnerAdditionalFieldDefinitionId`) and `which field carries the size estimate` (`SizeEstimateAdditionalFieldDefinitionId`) are declared on `Portfolio` (`Models/Portfolio.cs:19,21`) and are NOT reachable through `IWorkItemQueryOwner`, which is the parameter type of `FetchFingerprint.For`. If 01-02 wrote `For` against the interface alone, these two are the red, and the failure will read like a portfolio-wiring bug rather than a reach bug. The fix is the pattern match inside `For`, not a new overload and not a wider interface. Why they belong in the set at all, verified: `FeatureOwnerAdditionalFieldDefinitionId` is read at sync time by `JiraWorkTrackingConnector.GetOwningTeam:1020-1022` and `AzureDevOps...:940-942` and lands on the stored `Feature.OwningTeam` (`Jira...:1006,1011`); `SizeEstimateAdditionalFieldDefinitionId` by `GetEstimatedSize:1027-1029` / `947-950`, stored as `Feature.EstimatedSize`. Under delta an unchanged Feature is never re-derived, so the old owner and the old size survive the edit indefinitely - a wrong number with no error, which is the failure mode this whole slice exists to prevent. The connection reference is absent from this table for the same reason as the team one (DT5-9); scenario 16 covers it. Preflight and gates as in 01-01. One `[Ignore]`, ten cases, so skipped goes 29 -> 19.

steps.name: An edit to one entity is not an invalidation of the other
criteria: A team query edit leaves a portfolio on the same connection running Delta with 3 scanned / 0 fetched and downloading no Feature
A portfolio query edit leaves a team on the same connection running Delta with 3 scanned / 0 fetched and downloading nothing
The fingerprint is stored per entity, so neither edit reaches the other's stored value
Both were declared not-yet-falsifiable at DISTILL time and are re-run here, after both halves exist, which is the point at which they start guarding something
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.6, contract shape `unbounded-preservation` on both - each claims an absence. DISTILL classified both GUARD_NOT_YET_FALSIFIABLE and both PASSED at DISTILL time: with no fingerprint at all, `this edit invalidated nothing` was true for the trivial reason. Their positive controls are scenarios 3 and 4, which are now green, so this is the moment they become real. Un-ignore, RUN, and if green record the run rather than inventing work - `WorkItemService.cs` is listed as where a fix would land, not as a promise of an edit. WHAT THEY FORBID, and it is a shape somebody will reach for: hanging the fingerprint off the CONNECTION, or sharing one per connection, so that every team edit costs every portfolio on that connection a full re-download. ADR-140 chose one column on the shared base `WorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner`, inherited by both, precisely so the invalidation is per entity. Note the related design point ADR-140 accepted and these two do NOT contradict: a change to the CONNECTION does fan out to every entity on it - passively, each entity noticing at its own next cycle when it recomputes its own fingerprint, rather than as an N-entity write at connection-save time. Scenario 7 is that case; these two are about entity-scoped edits. PROVE THE GUARD CAN FAIL before committing: temporarily make the team's stored fingerprint the one the portfolio compares against (or vice versa), confirm the relevant scenario reds AND that nothing else in the fixture changes, then revert and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows no production file modified. A guard whose probe has not been re-run in the tree it ships into is a guard on nothing - the slice-03 phase 05 lesson. C# note from the ledger: `if (false)` cannot be used to park a probe, `TreatWarningsAsErrors` turns CS0162 unreachable-code into a build error. Preflight and gates as in 01-01; two `[Ignore]`s, one case each, so skipped goes 19 -> 17.

steps.name: The free list, re-run against a fingerprint that could have invalidated
criteria: All sixteen cases run Delta with 3 scanned / 0 fetched and issue zero downloads of any kind

The team's ten cover wait states, a blocked rule, both staleness thresholds, a named cycle time, the service level expectation, the system WIP limit, the throughput window, feature WIP and how estimates are read
The portfolio's six cover wait states, the staleness threshold, the assumed feature size, the states sized by that assumption, the percentile that derives it, and the service level expectation
The sixteen results are read, not assumed: the run output is recorded in the commit message
Not one of the sixteen edits moves the stored fingerprint
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.3 / KPI-4, contract shape `unbounded-preservation`. THESE GO LAST AND MUST BE RE-RUN AND READ, NOT ASSUMED. DISTILL classified both GUARD_NOT_YET_FALSIFIABLE and both passed on arrival - 10/10 and 6/6 - because with no fingerprint at all, `this edit invalidated nothing` is true for the trivial reason. They only start guarding something once a fingerprint exists that COULD have invalidated, which is now. Their positive controls are scenarios 3 and 4. WHAT THEY CATCH is the exact failure the slice brief names as the honest-but-wasteful collapse: `any settings save invalidates`. That answer is safe, it passes scenarios 1-8 and 11-17, and it spends the entire win - an admin who learns that every save is expensive stops tuning, which is worse than the original problem. Sixteen cases going green here is the only evidence the slice kept its second promise. So: un-ignore both, run the filtered suite, and PASTE THE COUNTS INTO THE COMMIT MESSAGE. If any case reds, the fingerprint is reading something the guard's decision table marks `Nothing` - the fix is in `For(...)`, and the offending property already has a row in the table explaining why it is free, so read that row before widening anything. The blocked-rule case (`a blocked rule`) is the interesting one and its answer is already recorded: it stays free, because `blockedItemService.IsBlocked(workItem, team)` (`WorkItemService.cs:290,293`) reads the STORED item, so re-deriving needs no remote call. The known gap that follows from that - the delta loop only visits downloaded items, so a rule edit does not re-open a quiet item's spell until it next moves - is REAL, is documented in the slice brief under `Known limitation this slice does not close`, and belongs to the ADR-141 / DDD-4 derivation pass. Do not fix it here by putting blocked rules in the fingerprint: that buys a local derivation with a full remote download and spends exactly the win these sixteen cases protect. Preflight and gates as in 01-01. Two `[Ignore]`s carrying sixteen cases between them, so skipped goes 17 -> 1 - the last skip in the slice is G1, which 04-04 takes.

steps.name: The property surface is closed, and the guard says so
criteria: Every operator-editable property across the query owners and the connection they point at is either registered in the fingerprint or on the exclusion list with its reason attached - nothing undecided
G1 runs un-ignored and green, in a commit of its own
G1 is proven able to fail: a throwaway property on the query-owner surface reds it and reds nothing else, and is removed again
The whole slice-05 filter runs with every specification un-ignored: 49 total, 49 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed
The full backend suite is green, with the slice's un-ignored specifications now counted as passing rather than skipped
steps.implementation_notes: AC-5.4 / DDD-8 / DT5-13, contract shape `pure-function`. THIS GETS ITS OWN COMMIT PRECISELY BECAUSE IT PASSES TODAY. G1 walks the operator-editable property surface of `WorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner`, `Team`, `Portfolio` and `WorkTrackingSystemConnection` and finds everything already decided - because DISTILL is what decided it. Taking it in its own step records the transition from ignored to enforced instead of letting it arrive silently inside a later test-infrastructure change, which is how a guard quietly becomes decoration. What it actually guards is the NEXT connector option somebody adds: a fetch-shaping property that is neither registered nor excluded makes the fingerprint drift, and a stale fingerprint means delta serves a stale result set with every test green - wrong numbers, no error. That is the slice's learning hypothesis, and AC-5.4 is why it is an acceptance criterion rather than a nice-to-have. RE-RUN THE FALSIFICATION PROBE IN THIS TREE, do not trust DISTILL's. DISTILL's is recorded and is the shape to repeat: add a throwaway `public string? ProbeOnlyDelete { get; set; }` to `WorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner`, run the slice-05 filter, confirm G1 fails with `Undecided properties: ProbeOnlyDelete` and that the failed count moves by exactly one - nothing else in the filter changes - then remove the property and confirm the tree returns. A guard whose probe has not been re-run in the tree it ships into is a guard on nothing. `git status --porcelain` must show no production file modified before you commit. Remember the collateral trap while the probe property exists: it is not mapped and has no migration, so it will not red the six migration tests, but if you are ever tempted to make it a real column, `Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/TestHelpers/HistoricalSchemaPatch.cs` needs a row or `DeliveryMetricSnapshotDayKeyMigrationTests` and `BlockedRuleSetMigrationTests` go red across two fixtures and two providers for a reason that has nothing to do with the change. `FetchFingerprint.cs` is listed as where a fix would land if G1 turns up something undecided; no edit is expected. ArchUnitNET cannot express this - it constrains types and dependencies, not property membership - which is why both guards are reflection assertions living in `Architecture/` beside the twenty ArchUnit seam tests, categorised `epic-5687-faster-updates` / `slice-05` but NOT `acceptance` (DT5-7). SLICE CLOSE-OUT, all in this commit or immediately after it: run the whole filter `dotnet test Lighthouse.sln --filter "TestCategory=slice-05&TestCategory=epic-5687-faster-updates"` and expect 49/49 with zero skips; run the full `dotnet test` and confirm 0 failed (baseline was 4786 passed / 49 skipped, and the 49 skips are now passes); run `cd Lighthouse.Backend && dotnet build` for zero warnings; then the mandatory analyzer preflight `dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore`, filtered with `{ git diff --name-only <base>; git status --porcelain | awk '{print $2}'; } | grep '\.cs$' | sort -u` so the new `FetchFingerprintTest.cs` is not invisible to the filter. Known flakes, not regressions: `JiraWriteBackTest.WriteDate_DifferentDate_...` under full-suite load and `ReleaseService` failing in a block of exactly ten. A release-note line is OWED at slice close for the narrowed purge - flag it, do not write it.
